# R01 — Isolate regression startup and preserve failure evidence

Priority: P0. Prerequisites: none. Unblocks R02, R03, and R05.
Workspace: `/Users/tyler/Documents/GitHub/stair-dismount`; target Godot 4.7.2 Compatibility.
This card authorizes implementation of this task only, followed by its acceptance checks.
The project has no Git history; inspect any newly added AGENTS.md before changing files.
Use `br --db /Users/tyler/Documents/GitHub/stair-dismount/.beads/beads.db` for tracking.
Claim the mapped R01 bead; do not initialize another tracker or require a Git repository.

## Game context and confirmed failure

STAIR // WRECK has MENU, READY, RUN, CRASH, RESULTS, and REPLAY phases.
Three routes bank their best insurance claims toward a $600,000 treatment fund.
`scenes/main.tscn` starts `scripts/main.gd`, which builds the world, rider, HUD, and audio.
The normal record is `user://records.json`; its production contents must remain untouched.
`tools/test.sh:12` currently supplies `--test-mode` to thirteen headless suites.
`scripts/main.gd:82` overrides every supplied pre-ready path with shared `builds/test_records.json`.
`scripts/main.gd:89` loads immediately, before several suites choose their own filenames.
Examples are `tests/test_inputs.gd:32–35` and `tests/test_playability.gd:158–161`.
The startup probe assigned an isolated `[11,22,33]` fixture before adding the scene.
It instead loaded `[46895,40536,56646]` from that shared test record.
This is confirmed startup contamination, not proof that all previous assertions were false.
The existing runner also accepts a zero exit without a completion marker and has no deadline.
Preserve meaningful physical, accounting, and dispatched-input assertions while repairing these seams.

## Scope, ownership, and rationale

Own `tools/test.sh`, a small bounded-process helper, and test startup/fixture plumbing.
Own only startup argument/save-path selection in `scripts/main.gd`; R02 owns record semantics.
Update affected direct-test command documentation when it changes, including validation instructions.
Do not edit collision thresholds, camera policy, payout rules, or native presentation here.
Keep original `builds/repair_audit/` probes and their failing logs as baseline evidence.
The rationale is that later repairs need trustworthy cold-start fixtures and bounded executions.
Increasing assertion totals or making every suite use a mock game would not provide that trust.
Coordinate the shared main.gd writer explicitly; readiness does not permit concurrent edits there.

## Required startup contract

Parse `--records-path=<path>` from Godot user arguments before any record read.
Explicit CLI path wins over a pre-ready injected path, which wins over test-mode defaults.
Normal `user://records.json` is selected only when no explicit override/test fixture exists.
`--test-mode` must never replace an explicit destination, regardless of argument order.
Multiple conflicting explicit overrides or an empty/malformed override fail clearly.
An inaccessible explicit destination remains that destination; never fall back to the user's record.
Accept an absolute isolated filename so packaged native tests can use normal presentation safely.
The override selects storage only; it must not imply automation, headless mode, or muted audio.
Preserve `--test-mode`, `--capture`, and `--self-check` behavior with documented path precedence.
Capture/self-check use isolated storage when no explicit override exists and never a user profile.
If a direct test-mode launch has no override, allocate a fresh project-local per-process fixture.
Construct/create its parent before loading; do not reuse the old shared test filename.
The harness allocates `builds/test_runs/<run-id>/<suite>/` and passes its absolute record path.
Suite fixture creation and selection happen before `root.add_child(game)` triggers `_ready()`.
Remove late hardcoded assignments that redirect saves away from the harness-selected fixture.
Provide one reusable fixture helper rather than independent boot-order logic in each suite.
The reopened persistence scenario uses a fresh process/startup fixture, not only manual load twice.
Keep an explicit negative fixture for missing parents so R02 can test save-open failure.

## Required runner contract

Keep `tools/test.sh` as the documented entry point and honor `GODOT_BIN`.
Add `tools/run_bounded.py` or an equivalently small documented portable process helper.
Its public CLI accepts `--timeout-seconds`, `--log`, then `--` and the argument-vector command.
Use argument vectors, not shell interpolation; preserve spaces in project/engine/fixture paths.
Each run captures combined output, process exit, elapsed time, timeout, and command identity.
Run a child process group; on deadline terminate it, wait briefly, then kill remaining children.
Initial limits: import 180 seconds and each suite 180 seconds; record any bounded override.
Permit explicit 10–600 second developer overrides; neither zero nor an infinite timeout is valid.
The timeout negative fixture uses a short internal deadline so verification does not stall.
Require exactly one expected `NAME: N checks, 0 failures` completion marker per suite.
The initial registry maps thirteen scripts to RULES, INJURIES, INPUTS, GAME, ROUTES, PLAYABILITY,
UI, AUDIO, SKATING, CRASHBREAKER, RIDER_SKIN, TRAFFIC, and CAMERA; suffix telemetry is permitted.
Each registry entry specifies script, expected summary name, and timeout. Later tasks register
their new regression suites explicitly and publish their names; every registered suite is mandatory.
Unknown/duplicate/wrong-name markers cannot satisfy another suite. Test fourteenth-suite registration,
its missing marker, and a valid marker from the wrong suite.
Missing, duplicate, wrong-name, malformed, zero-check, or nonzero-failure summaries fail the run.
Do not freeze old assertion totals as an oracle; added meaningful checks can change counts.
Reject SCRIPT ERROR, parse/compile errors, FAIL markers, reported leaks, and unexpected engine errors.
The known macOS certificate diagnostic may be narrowly classified by its exact condition/location.
Do not whitelist all ERROR lines or an arbitrary surrounding block that could hide a later failure.
Engine nonzero exit and timeout fail even when a success-looking summary exists.
Generate a run result JSON from actual outputs, not static hand-maintained counts.
Include engine version, run ID, input-source digest, suite identities/counts, and artifact paths.
Publish summary success only after every expected suite completed with the required checks.
Do not run imports/tests concurrently against shared logs or the same fixture directory.

## Reproduction and independent acceptance

From the workspace, use `/opt/homebrew/bin/godot --headless --path "$PWD"`.
Append `--script res://builds/repair_audit/startup_path_probe.gd -- --test-mode` for the baseline.
Before repair its effective path is the shared test file; retain that original output.
Add a new explicit-path cold-start regression without rewriting the baseline to claim success.
Use a poison shared test file only inside an isolated project copy or preserved fixture scope.
The passing oracle is the supplied `[11,22,33]`, mute, and hat values, not a loader-generated value.
Test CLI order, injected-path precedence, capture/self-check precedence, and invalid override handling.
Cold-start two different fixtures concurrently and show neither observes the other's scores.
Check a fresh process reads its selected v1 fixture without calling `load_records()` a second time.
Runner subprocess fixtures cover success, early zero exit, zero checks, wrong/missing/duplicate marker,
nonzero exit after a marker, script-error zero exit, an unexpected ERROR, and a child-process hang.
Show the known certificate diagnostic alone passes and the same log plus a script error fails.
Confirm timeout cleanup leaves no fixture child alive and caller receives a nonzero status.
Use controlled fixture directories; do not create, inspect, chmod, rename, or delete the real user save.
The proof of no user-directory access is the effective startup path/event trace, not reading that directory.
Run the affected startup/persistence/input cases, then the existing full suite once after plumbing stabilizes.
Preserve the preceding 1,780-assertion report as historical evidence, not the new expected total.

## Handoff and completion

Write `docs/repair/evidence/R01.md` with failing/passing commands, paths, parser cases, and limits.
Document the bounded-helper CLI, fixture helper, and startup precedence for later fresh agents.
R02 must receive structured startup selection and a reliable isolated-process record fixture.
R03/R05 must receive preserved reproductions and the bounded runner without gameplay changes.
Close R01 only after cold-start isolation and runner negative cases pass with actual engine evidence.
A new wrapper file, mocked success marker, or larger assertion count alone does not complete the task.
Keep all generated run outputs under builds; do not export test fixtures into the game PCK.

## Failure handling and rollback

Before changing startup/runner plumbing, preserve source copies and the original failure logs.
If isolation or timeout cleanup fails, restore only this task's own changed files and keep diagnostics.
Do not restore over another agent's edits, modify physical rules, or touch player records during rollback.
close_reason: Cold-start isolation and runner contracts verified: STARTUP279 INPUTS39 plus21 negative controls; strict full entry correctly rejected sandbox editor errors; full-runtime/native gates remain R12/R14. Evidence docs/repair/evidence/R01.md.

title: R02 — Recover and commit records with truthful funding state
description:
# R02 — Recover and commit records with truthful funding state

Priority: P0. Prerequisite: R01. Unblocks R10 and integration R12.
Workspace: `/Users/tyler/Documents/GitHub/stair-dismount`; Godot 4.7.2 Compatibility.
Read R01's evidence/fixture contract and inspect any new AGENTS.md before implementation.
Use `br --db /Users/tyler/Documents/GitHub/stair-dismount/.beads/beads.db` and claim R02.
This card authorizes this repair and its checks; it does not authorize a new progression model.

## Context, source, and confirmed triggers

The three-route crash game banks each route's best claim toward a $600,000 treatment goal.
The phases are MENU, READY, RUN, CRASH, RESULTS, and REPLAY; replay cannot earn money.
`scripts/main.gd:109–122` loads records by mutating live arrays during unchecked conversions.
`scripts/main.gd:124–126` silently writes over the only file and returns no status.
`scripts/main.gd:459–465` announces a secured best claim even when that write fails.
Mute and hat callers at `scripts/main.gd:202,223` share the same unchecked save path.
`scripts/game_hud.gd:344–373` derives funding/ending text from the current in-memory scores.
A score array `[123,{},456]` causes a script error after applying only its first value.
A string mute field causes another conversion error; future version 99 is rewritten as v2.
Truncated JSON is later replaced by zeros when an ordinary preference save occurs.
The settlement probe reports RESULTS and $200,000 secured with no destination file.
These are real isolated reproductions, not observed corruption of the player's existing profile.
Existing tests in `tests/test_inputs.gd:105–133` cover only valid v1/v2 writable round trips.

## Scope and architectural rationale

Own the records service, main.gd record/settlement integration, and targeted regression fixtures.
Keep a small service boundary, for example `scripts/records_store.gd`, with checked results.
R10 owns complete recovery/funding layout; provide correct state and minimal truthful wording now.
Do not change physical scoring, the treatment goal, route availability, or one-breaker accounting.
One main.gd writer at a time is required even when R03/R05 are dependency-ready.
Why: whole-candidate validation prevents partial loads, and checked commits prevent false funding.
Keep session progress when storage fails; discarding earned claims would replace one bug with another.

## Candidate schema and loading result

Current serialized v2 fields remain `version`, `best_scores`, `legacy_scores`, `muted`, and `hat`.
`best_scores` and `legacy_scores` each contain exactly three route values in route order.
Scores must be numeric, finite, integral, nonnegative, and no greater than 999999999.
Allow legitimate JSON integer-valued numeric representation; reject strings, Booleans, nulls, fractions, and containers.
Support exactly version 1 and version 2; missing version means the established v1 legacy format.
Malformed version values and unsupported versions must not be coerced into a supported number.
For v1, valid `best_scores` become legacy scores and current treatment bests start at zero.
For v2, valid current bests load independently from optional historical legacy values.
Malformed optional mute defaults false, malformed hat defaults 0, and malformed optional legacy defaults zeros.
A malformed optional field must not invalidate an otherwise valid best-score candidate or raise a script error.
For v1, an optional malformed legacy field must never overwrite the migrated valid historical scores.
Validate into temporary typed values; commit all active state only after the whole required candidate passes.
Return `load_state`: `missing`, `loaded`, `recoverable`, `corrupt`, `inaccessible`, or `unsupported`.
Include candidate/default state, diagnostic code, protected original path, and valid backup candidate if present.
Missing means a clean first run; inaccessible/corrupt/unsupported never masquerade as missing.
Retain unsupported newer data byte-for-byte and make that profile read-only for this older client.
No preference toggle or new claim may downgrade it, remove unknown fields, or replace it with defaults.
Keep corrupt required-score input protected; offer a validated backup rather than silently applying zeros.
Expose `recover_backup()` as an explicit operation for R10; do not invent an automatic destructive reset.
Also expose `recover_fresh()` only for an explicit player choice when required-score data is corrupt
and no valid backup exists. Quarantine original bytes uniquely before replacement; preservation
failure leaves protected bytes/session progress intact. Unsupported future profiles are never reset.
Both recovery actions use checked commits and merge per-route session maxima. Treat validated
recovered scores as the contribution baseline: restoring saved money alone is not new earnings
and does not emit a newly-funded ending; only earned increases above that baseline can do so.
If recovery is accepted, preserve the rejected original under a unique local quarantine name first.
Failure to preserve it prevents replacement and yields a checked error; never overwrite a quarantine file.
Reconcile an accepted backup with session improvements by per-route maximum, never additive replay credit.

## Checked saving and recovery contract

`commit(candidate)` returns `ok`, diagnostic code, durable snapshot, and pending candidate.
Serialize a fully validated candidate into a unique sibling temporary file in the same directory.
Check open, store, flush/close status as available in the local runtime, and read/validate the temporary bytes.
Retain the last validated primary as backup before replacing it; do not rotate corrupt input into the good backup.
Inspect every copy/rename/replacement result and keep old recoverable data until the commit is verified.
Define the commit point. Return `uncertain` if replacement may have succeeded but validation failed;
withhold secured wording and keep the pending candidate. Retry rereads primary/backup before
another write and reconciles complete validated snapshots with the previously acknowledged baseline.
Emit one contribution only after acknowledged reconciliation, never once for each write attempt.
If an initially inaccessible profile becomes readable, validate/migrate it before merging session
maxima; do not overwrite its existing funding with session defaults simply because retry is now possible.
Verify Godot 4.7/filesystem operation behavior locally; do not assert universal power-loss durability.
Do not use delete-primary-then-rename as an alleged atomic replacement without preserving recovery.
Cold startup handles leftover temporary/backup files with a documented deterministic selection policy.
An uncommitted temp cannot become secured funding merely because it contains a higher score.
Reject writes while the selected profile is unsupported/inaccessible or unresolved corruption remains protected.
Do not silently switch save paths; a failed selected path remains a visible pending-storage condition.
Maintain the session candidate on open/write/replace failure and expose an explicit retry operation.
Preference edits join the pending complete candidate so subsequent success saves both claims and preferences.
After successful commit clear the pending state and use the exact validated committed snapshot.
Repeated retries, finish callbacks, and weaker claims must not add a contribution twice.

## Durable versus session interface for main/HUD

Keep `best_scores` as durable per-route bests and add `session_best_scores` for earned session maxima.
`fund_total()` returns only durable funding; provide `session_fund_total()` separately.
Add `records_status`, `pending_save`, and diagnostic/recovery fields with documented typed values.
Track `session_improvement` separately from `last_money_secured`, which means newly committed durable increase.
Compute a durable contribution from committed maxima versus the prior durable snapshot, never from call count.
On a failed claim save, results retain the earned claim/session best but show no newly secured amount.
Only a successful commit that crosses the goal can produce the newly-funded ending.
Expose a consumable committed-contribution/goal-crossing event so a preference-triggered retry is handled once.
After failure, replay/navigation/retry cannot convert pending money into durable money implicitly.
Sound/ending integrations receive the durable crossing event, not a repeated comparison against session totals.
R10 receives recovery actions, pending-save retry action, durable/session figures, and actionable diagnostics.
Maintain normal loaded preferences and hats even when no new claim is earned.
Do not disable play merely because an old profile is protected; allow clearly labeled session-only progress.

## Reproduction and acceptance

Use R01's `--records-path=<absolute fixture>` cold-start selection; never access the real user profile.
Baseline probe: `--script res://builds/repair_audit/records_probe.gd -- --probe=invalid_element`.
Other modes are `coercion`, `future_version`, `malformed`, and `open_failure`; retain their original logs.
Baseline settlement: `--script res://builds/repair_audit/settlement_probe.gd` on the isolated missing parent.
Run through `/opt/homebrew/bin/godot --headless --path "$PWD"` with bounded logs under builds.
Create explicit fixtures for valid v1/v2, missing fields/version, boundaries, malformed required/optional fields,
unreadable primary, unsupported future version, corrupt primary with/without valid backup, and stale temporary files.
Test invalid score positions first/middle/last; no scenario may partly alter the loaded score arrays.
Cover no-backup fresh recovery, v1 backup migration, already-funded backup recovery, and recovery
plus a session improvement. Recovery without new earnings must not produce a new-funded event.
Assert explicit known fixture values and file bytes; do not generate expected results with the production parser.
Inject/check failure before temp creation, during write, after verification, during backup, and during replacement.
Separately inject successful primary replacement followed by failed readback/validation.
Require uncertain status, unchanged acknowledged funds, and retained pending candidate/baseline.
After reads recover, recognize the written candidate before another replacement; acknowledge
one earned contribution and none on a second retry.
Recovery fixture: backup [500000,0,0], session [550000,0,0], corrupt primary. Fail post-replace
readback, then reconcile: contribution 50000, fund 550000, and no goal crossing; restored funding
is not new earnings. Initially unreadable primary [100000,500000,0] with session [200000,0,0]
becomes readable: baseline is already funded, commit [200000,500000,0], contribution 100000,
and no newly-funded event. Use explicit expected arrays/event counts, not production event math.
Each failure leaves a complete recoverable committed record and a pending session candidate when appropriate.
Use deterministic failure seams or isolated filesystem fixtures; permission-only tests can be bypassed by admin users.
Run a fresh process after failure/recovery/success and prove the selected durable state and preference values.
A $200,000 failing settlement shows session improvement but zero new secured contribution and no ending.
Repair the storage condition, retry twice, and prove one durable contribution and one crossing event at most.
Weaker retries and replay leave durable maxima unchanged; optional-field repair preserves valid claim scores.
Future-version/corrupt protected originals remain byte-for-byte recoverable through mute/hat/play operations.
Run targeted records/input/playability checks after the change; R12 later owns the integrated complete regression.

## Completion and handoff

Write `docs/repair/evidence/R02.md` with schema, error/result types, replacement behavior, and actual proof.
Document platform limits honestly; process-interruption tests do not prove survival of arbitrary power loss.
Give R10 the exact durable/session/recovery interface and R12 the cold-start/failure matrix.
Close R02 only after recovery, failed-save truthfulness, idempotent retry, and clean restart all pass.
close_reason: Independent review reproduced recovery-baseline accounting bug; corrected with actual before332/2 and after332/0 plus integratedUI1400/0 for preference/newclaim paths. Evidence docs/repair/evidence/R02.md.

title: R03 — Make modal focus and gameplay input authoritative
description:
# R03 — Make modal focus and gameplay input authoritative

Priority: P0. Prerequisite: R01. Unblocks: R10, R11, R12.
Workspace: `/Users/tyler/Documents/GitHub/stair-dismount`; Godot 4.7.2 Compatibility.
This card authorizes an input/modal repair after R01 closes, not unrelated gameplay changes.
Read any newly added AGENTS.md before editing; the audited workspace has no Git repository.
Reserve the shared `main.gd` writer slot before editing alongside R02 or R05.

## Background and independent reproduction

`scenes/main.tscn` loads `scripts/main.gd`, which owns six phases and pause flags.
`scripts/game_hud.gd` creates Buttons whose signals call gameplay methods directly.
The player charges in READY, rides in RUN, bails into CRASH, then reaches RESULTS/REPLAY.
Exactly one Shift crashbreaker is available per attempt; input repair must preserve it.
The confirmed F03 incident lets focused underlying Buttons act through help or pause.
Focus FILE A CLAIM in MENU, press H, then Enter: the current game enters READY.
Focus pose 3 in READY while pose 1 is selected; H, Enter changes pose under help.
Esc, Enter similarly changes the underlying focused pose while pause remains visible.
F04: focus the live II Button in RUN, hold Tab; slow motion does not engage.
Remove GUI focus and hold the identical Tab: `slow_motion=true`, `time_rate=.25`.
These observations used actual `Input.parse_input_event`, not direct callback invocation.
Reproduction source: `builds/repair_audit/state_ui_probe.gd`; observations: its JSON/log.
`docs/repair/audit_state_ui.md` UI-01/UI-02 contains the exact captured conditions.
Relevant source: `main.gd:131-136,176-179,190-199,206-242` and `game_hud.gd:108-116,289-313`.
The mouse backdrops block clicks but leave keyboard focus outside the visible modal.
The `_unhandled_input` guard cannot stop GUI signals that already consumed Enter or Tab.

## Chosen contract and rationale

Use one action eligibility policy for keyboard events, HUD signals and automation calls.
Put the policy near the phase owner; HUD should request actions rather than bypass it.
Do not solve this by removing Button keyboard focus: menu accessibility must remain.
Track a single visible modal kind NONE/PAUSE/HELP and its explicit return context.
Opening help from a running phase pauses; closing it restores that same phase.
Opening help from MENU or RESULTS does not start a run or reset its result.
If help opens while already paused, closing help returns to the existing pause modal.
Opening pause or help clears charge and slow-motion latches, preserving accumulated charge.
A Space release launches only if its matching press began in eligible READY.
Window focus loss clears all held action latches; return requires a fresh gameplay press.
This prevents a stale release or GUI callback from causing an unexpected launch.
Polling W/A/D and arrow movement must also require active window focus and no modal.
Clear eligibility on phase replacement, retry, route change and replay entry/exit.
Use `get_tree().paused` and the existing `is_paused` flag consistently in every transition.
Preserve the .55/.25/.18 rate policy; R05 later changes clock ownership, not input meaning.

Focus loss in READY/RUN/CRASH/REPLAY enters the existing pause state unless a modal already owns
suspension. Record a focus-suspension latch even when HELP already owns suspension. Focus gain
does not resume. After loss from a live phase during HELP, closing HELP returns to PAUSE,
and only Resume clears the latch. Existing PAUSE return stays PAUSE; MENU/RESULTS keep their
phase and ordinary help return. All held/polled gameplay keys require
release/repress after focus loss, not merely a cleared event latch.

## Action and focus interfaces

Document an explicit phase/action table beside the centralized dispatch implementation.
Mute is a global presentation/preference action in every phase, including PAUSE/HELP.
M uses the authoritative policy, cannot launch/resume/change phase, and respects R02 protected
records/pending state. Help H toggles the active help panel without bypassing focus suspension.
MENU: route/play/help/mute and Button keyboard navigation; no charge, bail or breaker.
READY: pose/hat/steering/charge/camera plus pause/help/retry; no breaker or filing.
RUN: push/steering/bail/held slow/camera plus pause/help/retry; no pose/hat changes.
CRASH: aftertouch/breaker/held slow/file/camera plus pause/help/retry; no charge.
RESULTS: retry/next/route/replay/help/mute and Button navigation; no live gameplay action.
REPLAY: replay camera/retry/pause/help/mute; no live impulses, file or payout action.
Visible PAUSE/HELP controls are the only GUI owners while those modals are open.
Tab and Shift-Tab cycle only the visible modal's enabled controls; Enter activates that owner.
Live Space and Tab receive ownership before GUI navigation in their eligible phases.
Handle press and release together; do not rely on `_unhandled_input` for those actions.
MENU/RESULTS keep ordinary GUI Tab/Enter navigation when no modal is visible.
Restore the previous focus on close only when it is still valid, enabled and visible.
Otherwise choose the phase's first sensible Button or release focus in live gameplay.
Publish action eligibility and modal-transition behavior for R10 UI and R11 audio consumers.
Avoid renaming persistence fields or changing save semantics; R02 owns that boundary.

## Implementation steps

1. Consume R01's pre-_ready unique fixture and bounded test-process harness.
2. Preserve the current reproductions and confirm their expected failure before editing.
3. Route HUD play/pose/retry/route/resume/help requests through the action policy.
4. Introduce coherent modal entry/exit and focus capture, trap and restoration.
5. Replace fragmented pause/help toggles with explicit transitions and return context.
6. Give eligible held actions pre-GUI ownership; preserve normal menu navigation.
7. Cancel latches on focus loss, modal entry and phase reset, including matching-release state.
8. Gate movement polling while unfocused so a still-held physical key cannot resume motion.
9. Verify direct methods cannot bypass the policy while preserving valid automation/test calls.
10. Extend existing dispatcher tests or add `tests/test_modal_inputs.gd` to R01's runner.
11. Record the public policy and regressions in task evidence, with no fabricated native claims.

## Independent tests and commands
Dispatch M in READY/RUN/CRASH with a focused live Button and under PAUSE/HELP. Require one
mute change per fresh non-echo press, with phase/modal/charge/breaker/funding unchanged.
R11/R14 retain actual player-state and audible checks.

Dispatch focus loss/gain during HELP from every live phase, then close via H, Escape, and Button.
Require PAUSE, unchanged clocks/actors and no stale release until explicit Resume plus new input.
R14 repeats these with actual OS focus.


Use actual parsed key and pointer events plus `gui_get_focus_owner`; avoid direct callbacks.
Use unique save fixtures before adding the game to the tree and absolute log paths.
Run `GODOT_BIN=/opt/homebrew/bin/godot ./tools/test.sh` through R01's bounded runner.
Targeted tests should use `--headless --fixed-fps 60 --script tests/test_modal_inputs.gd`.
Their log path must be absolute under `builds/repair/R03/`, using R01's fixture argument.
Exercise focused underlying play/pose controls under H help and Esc pause.
Assert phase/pose/boosts/fund do not change; checking `charging=false` alone is insufficient.
Walk Tab and Shift-Tab for at least two complete modal cycles and check owner ancestry.
Enter on each visible modal action should perform exactly its documented transition.
In RUN/CRASH, test held Tab with every live Button focused and with no focus.
Accept exact engagement .25 unless a .18 impact pulse has documented higher priority.
On release, require the correct base rate within one render/physics update, not sticky slow.
Charge tests cover release without press, press under modal, press before focus loss and retry.
None may launch; a fresh valid READY press/release must launch exactly once.
Test both help entry routes: H and the real HOW TO WRECK Button.
Check MENU/READY/RUN/CRASH/RESULTS/REPLAY and help opened from an existing pause.
Assert modal visibility, tree pause, game pause and returned phase agree after every action.
Hold/repeat/release Shift around modal and replay transitions; never restore a spent charge.
Add a native focus-loss checklist for R14; headless synthetic events cannot prove OS releases.
Do not weaken existing input, campaign, hat or migration assertions to make this pass.

## Risks, rollback and done evidence

Overbroad pre-GUI capture can destroy menu accessibility or activate gameplay under help.
Double dispatch can launch/spend twice; mark an owned event handled exactly once.
Nested help can incorrectly resume an already paused attempt; the saved return context is required.
Rollback only this input/modal change from the preserved source snapshot; retain evidence/tests.
Do not reset a player's scores or replace the game engine to recover from an input regression.
Done requires passing independent dispatcher cases, unchanged one-use/accounting behavior,
and a recorded phase/action table plus focus/modal transition matrix for downstream tasks.
Attach commands, fixture paths, failure-before/pass-after logs and changed-file list.
Native focus-loss observations remain an explicit R14 gate, not a claimed headless success.
R10 may then build coherent recovery/viewport UI; R11 may rely on pause/modal transitions.
close_reason: Authoritative modal/input actions implemented, real parsed input MODAL_INPUTS410 INPUTS39 and updated UI635 pass. Evidence docs/repair/evidence/R03.md; native focus matrix separate.

# R04 — Ground skating and sweep real obstacle geometry

Priority: P1. Dependencies: **R05**. Unblocks: **R07, R08, R12**.
Workspace: `/Users/tyler/Documents/GitHub/stair-dismount`.
This card implements repairs after dependency acceptance; drafting this card made no gameplay edit.

## Context a fresh agent needs

STAIR // WRECK is a Godot 4.7.2 Compatibility skateboard crash game with three routes.
`scenes/main.tscn` creates `main.gd`; `world_builder.gd` builds real tread/prop bodies.
MENU/READY select a pose and lane; RUN scripts the riding Node3D; CRASH owns the ragdoll.
Space charges/releases launch and deliberately bails; W kicks on the flat; A/D steers.
The current solver is 90 Hz. R05 owns clocks, interpolation, placement reset, and presentation.
Rider parts and board are imported models; preserve the models and $600,000 funding rules.
There is currently no Git repository or AGENTS.md; check for newly added instructions first.
Read completed R05 evidence and its exact APIs before editing shared `main.gd`.
Reserve `main.gd`, `rider.gd`, and any shared builder edits; readiness does not permit concurrent writes.

## Evidence and goal

F01: `main.gd:303` uses max(prop width, length)/2 on both horizontal axes.
The 1.85 × 3.3 m taxi from `world_builder.gd:193–196` therefore has a false 1.95 m side envelope.
`physics_report.json.near_miss` shows 0.458182 m actual rider/hull clearance but CRASH and armed taxi.
F02: `main.gd:291–292` caps vertical following at 9 m/s while Port requires more at high speed.
The measured Port outside approach floats 0.620 m when coasting and 0.920 m with runway kicks.
`audit_physics.md` finding 1/2 and `probe_physics.gd` preserve the original failures and limitations.
Remove phantom strikes and cumulative hovering while retaining fast, playable stair descent.

## Chosen boundary and rationale

Keep the arcade riding controller, its heading, speed/drag/kick rules, and existing ragdoll.
Use explicit physics geometry queries; do not convert the game to wheel suspension or CharacterBody3D.
Riding obstruction queries target prop layer 2; layer 1 treads provide support and later ragdoll injury.
Real stairs must not become a crash obstacle at every descending nose.
Keep existing lateral limits and manual/automatic bail behavior unless this acceptance exposes an error.
Shape geometry may be a small bounded board/rider proxy set following the selected pose and heading.
Document its dimensions and padding; a huge pose-independent bounding box is not an acceptable substitute.
Use current CollisionShape3D geometry/transform for props, including rotated and tipped bodies.
No change to property values, injury payout, fund accounting, or direct activation momentum is needed.

## Interface contract

Add a focused skating-query helper, or equally small functions under the existing owner.
Its obstruction input contains previous/next world riding transforms and immutable proxy shape transforms.
Its output is empty for no hit, otherwise `{collider, fraction, at, normal}` in world coordinates.
`fraction` is finite in [0,1]; select the earliest qualifying obstruction across all proxies.
The collider must be a currently valid unbroken non-traffic CrashProp from this route.
Queries do not arm, pay, spawn limbs, or advance clocks; `main.gd` owns the single resulting activation/bail.
Handle starting overlaps separately because `cast_motion()` ignores already overlapping query shapes.
Do not infer a contact from the broad-phase radius; filter a true overlap/sweep by its rider-contact policy.
Support placement returns the simulation root's grounded world height and resets with route/retry placement.
R05 presentation interpolation may smooth the display but must not change the authoritative riding transform.
R08 must receive the corrected world pose on the tick that bail begins.

## Implementation steps

1. Run the preserved taxi/Port reproductions using R01's isolated fixture before making changes.
2. Record support clearance per tick, first struck collider, sweep fraction, pose, heading, and timestep.
3. Extract/cache a few reusable riding proxy shapes; do not allocate dozens of new resources each tick.
4. Query initial overlap and motion to the proposed next pose against real prop geometry.
5. Resolve only the earliest qualifying obstruction, preserving one activation and one bail transition.
   Before activation/bail place the simulation root at the earliest accepted contact transform,
   with documented separation tolerance, and derive the R08 bail pose there, not at the proposed end.
   Exclude ineligible RIDs before sweeping or continue a bounded search past them.
   Substep heading changes with a maximum proxy-boundary travel of .10 m and angle of 5 degrees;
   within each substep use a conservative bound for the intermediate angular hull as well.
   Bounds select candidates; refine them against the actual oriented proxy before accepting contact.
   Contact-position/error tolerance is at most .002 m; .10 m/5 degrees are subdivision ceilings,
   not accepted error. Subdivide further when needed without reducing supported speed.
6. Correct support following from the authored stair profile or actual support queries.
7. Permit at most one riser's brief wheel bounce, then catch up before the next stair descent.
8. Keep support and cosmetic torso/leg smoothing distinct so smoothing cannot accumulate a physical gap.
9. Integrate R05's transform/reset ownership; avoid interpolated presentation poses feeding back into simulation.
10. Add targeted seam regressions and register them with R01's bounded runner.

## Independent acceptance oracle

Use PhysicsDirectSpaceState queries to actual CollisionShape3D bodies as the collision/support oracle.
The oracle must not call the new production hit helper or copy its radius/height formulas.
The preserved 0.458 m-clear TUCK taxi pass stays RUN with no activation, limb spawn, or payout.
Progressively inward passes cross the actual declared proxy/hull boundary and hit exactly once.
Test front/side taxi, thin domino, rotated/tipped prop, each pose, and both steering directions.
At supported maximum speed, a thin-obstacle sweep hits; a neighboring positive-clearance sweep misses.
An initially overlapping eligible prop bails once without relying on `cast_motion()` reporting the overlap.
Test an excluded first collider followed by a thin eligible obstruction, plus a mid-step turning hit.
Independently verify the first ragdoll pose starts at the accepted contact boundary within declared
separation tolerance; a hit count alone cannot establish that the rider did not tunnel past it.
Include a grazing turn with clear endpoints/sampled-orientation casts but independently sampled
actual-hull penetration over .002 m. Find it; a paired >.002 m-clear turn remains a miss.
Bracket earliest contact against a finer independent geometry sample, not the production refinement.
Measure the root-center wheel-ground reference using actual tread top hits, not production `surface_y()` alone.
Do not require four coplanar wheels to touch two different-height treads; inspect their bounded bounce separately.
On all three outside routes, minimum/full charge and real held W must never accumulate clearance over one rise.
Grounded support-reference clearance is within 0.03 m except a single-riser transition lasting at most 0.10 s.
After a transition the clearance must return within 0.03 m before another riser adds error.
Port's old 0.620/0.920 m maxima must fail this independent test and disappear after repair.
Deliberate late bail starts at the accepted support height; obstacle contacts still produce finite causal damage.
Check normal/slow clocks through R05's test matrix; solver-step changes may not skip thin props.
Do not improve pass rates by reducing top speed, increasing bounds, or dropping full-charge Port coverage.

## Commands and evidence

Use `/opt/homebrew/bin/godot`, absolute logs, unique record fixtures, and R01 per-process deadlines.
Create `tests/test_skating_contacts.gd` for the regression cases and register it in the bounded runner.
The direct debug invocation is:

```sh
/opt/homebrew/bin/godot --headless --path /Users/tyler/Documents/GitHub/stair-dismount --log-file /Users/tyler/Documents/GitHub/stair-dismount/builds/repair_audit/R04_contacts.log --script res://tests/test_skating_contacts.gd
```

Write before/after per-case JSON to `builds/repair_audit/R04_contacts.json` with observed clearance and contacts.
Native visuals are checked in R14; headless support evidence does not claim human-rated skating quality.

## Risks, rollback, and done

New proxies can replace false positives with false negatives; preserve inward/front positive controls.
Support changes can alter late traffic timing; preserve the actual A→B→C scenario without scripted credit.
Save a source copy/diff before edits; revert only this task's movement/query changes if acceptance fails.
Do not overwrite later agent work, production records, models, or the packaged app during rollback.

documented proxy/support tolerances, no unexpected script errors, R05 integration evidence,
and a passing contact-placement-to-existing-bail seam fixture. Publish accepted pose/reset APIs
and evidence for R08; completed downstream R08 evidence is not required to close R04.
Update completion evidence only after those outcomes exist; a helper stub or test-only patch is incomplete.

# R05 — Separate clocks and simulation from render presentation

Priority: P1.
Depends on: R01.
Unblocks: R04, R07, R08, R09, R06, R11.

## Context for a fresh implementer

Work in `/Users/tyler/Documents/GitHub/stair-dismount`.
This is a three-route Godot 4.7.2 Compatibility skateboard crash game.
The player charges, skates down stairs, bails into eleven rigid limbs and a board,
then uses exactly one crashbreaker to extend a physical property/traffic cascade.
Claims fund the best-score-per-route treatment story; preserve those game rules.
No project AGENTS.md or Git repository existed when this plan was written.
Read any governing instructions added since; do not create a Git repository for this task.
The implementation owner must reserve shared scripts before changing them.
R01 supplies isolated startup fixtures and a bounded regression runner.
Do not write a real player user:// save during a probe.

## Failure and rationale

`main.gd:494–500` derives wall time by dividing render delta by Engine.time_scale,
then changes that global scale in the same callback.
Impact callbacks also change the scale from physics processing.
That makes the provenance of a delta at a scale transition ambiguous.
`main.gd:328–329` discards sample-clock remainder, and recorded frames have no time.
`camera_clock_probe.json` independently measured .055 s sampling at crash rate .55,
while playback assumes .05 s; this is confirmed timing distortion, repaired in R06.
The project currently has 90 Hz physics and no automatic interpolation enabled.
Rider skin updates run in render and pose callbacks; inspect exact ownership before enabling it.
Headless probes cannot prove visible stutter, so the rendered smoothness gate is in R14.

Choose explicit clock domains and presentation ownership because slow motion magnifies
small timing inconsistencies; changing solver rates would alter the physical game.
Keep the 90 Hz physics rate and the existing four time rates initially.
Only change a rate after measured collision and presentation comparisons support it.

## Required clock interface

Define a small clock policy in existing code or a focused helper such as game_clock.gd.
Expose simulation elapsed for RUN and CRASH, presentation elapsed, and effective rate.
Simulation elapsed increments from the actual physics callback delta exactly once.
Presentation elapsed uses Time.get_ticks_usec monotonic samples with an explicit baseline.
Entering pause/help stops gameplay presentation timers and refreshes that baseline.
Resuming must not add the duration spent in a modal.
Handle first sample, route replacement, focus loss, and replay as explicit resets.
Focus suspension refreshes the wall-clock baseline while preserving accumulated run/crash time.
Physics, replay time, and action audio remain suspended until R03 Resume; fuses/idle/deadlines
do not accrue during focus suspension. MENU/RESULTS follow R03 without resetting campaign state.
The same suspension remains when HELP closes into focus-induced PAUSE; only Resume clears it.
Do not call sleep to synthesize normal frame duration.
Do not multiply physics delta by Engine.time_scale a second time.
Impact-left, impact-cooldown, and cascade camera focus use active presentation seconds.
Fuse countdowns, damage/contact cooldowns, and physical settlement use simulation seconds.
The maximum crash deadline remains 34 active presentation seconds.
The ordinary crash cap remains 16 simulated seconds, subject to R09's reason reporting.
The rate priority remains impact .18, held slow .25, crash .55, ordinary 1.0.
Pause prevents motion; time-scale and pause-tree state must agree after every transition.

## Presentation ownership

Simulation transforms are written by physics owners only during live play.
Automatic physics interpolation is enabled only after all transform writers are inventoried.
Camera and live visual-only helpers use a deliberate render presentation path.
Replay transforms are already interpolated manually and must opt out of automatic interpolation.
Avoid a second smoothing layer on the hero that introduces extra visual lag.
For bones driven by external rigid bodies, choose one explicit solution:
read interpolated body transforms in render and drive a non-interpolated visual skeleton,
or compute visual poses on physics ticks and validate skeleton interpolation support locally.
Prefer the first when the installed version cannot interpolate the custom bone writes correctly.
Do not write the same bone pose independently in both callbacks.
Document which transforms are simulation data and which are presentation data.
Reset interpolation after placement, bail transfer, retry, route change, and replay exit.
Never use a visually interpolated body transform as input to injury or contact scoring.

## Implementation sequence

1. Capture baseline time-policy traces at rates 1, .55, .25, and .18 using R01 fixtures.
2. Inventory main, rider, skin, traffic wheels, particles, and camera callback ownership.
3. Introduce the clock interface and replace ambiguous real_delta derivation.
4. Move rate changes through one authoritative policy at well-defined transitions.
5. Record monotonic simulation timestamps for R06 without assuming a sample frequency.
6. Choose and implement the body/skin presentation ownership described above.
7. Enable physics interpolation for eligible live actors and reset teleports explicitly.
8. Opt replay presentation out and leave physics bodies frozen throughout replay.
9. Run focused clock/state tests, then existing affected gameplay/skin suites.
10. Record unresolved native observations in the R14 handoff rather than claiming them passed.

## Independent acceptance cases

- Feed a known monotonic sequence across rate changes and verify presentation time exactly.
- Pause for a constructed long interval; resume timers without an accumulated jump.
- Assert simulation time equals the sum of supplied physics deltas within 1e-6 seconds.
- Drive impact and held Tab overlap; assert the documented rate priority at each boundary.
- Retry and change route after a slow crash; clocks, rate, impact state, and latches reset.
- Verify fuse progression is invariant for equal simulated elapsed at different render rates.
- Verify presentation cooldown duration is invariant for equal active wall elapsed.
- Verify a replay cannot advance live fuses, rules, forces, or crash deadlines.
- Use a temporary 10 Hz diagnostic to reveal interpolation ownership warnings locally.
- Restore the shipped 90 Hz setting before acceptance; do not ship the diagnostic tick rate.
- Compare native motion later at 30, 60, and high-refresh rendering without FPS promises.

Clock tests use a controlled clock input seam, not sleeps or Engine.time_scale division
copied from production; this gives an independent oracle without mocking physics contacts.
Use existing real Godot bodies for transform and route-reset integration cases.
Test commands follow R01's isolated runner; before it exists, use:
`/opt/homebrew/bin/godot --headless --path /Users/tyler/Documents/GitHub/stair-dismount --fixed-fps 60 --script builds/repair_audit/camera_clock_probe.gd --log-file /Users/tyler/Documents/GitHub/stair-dismount/builds/repair_audit/camera_clock_probe.log`.
Preserve this baseline reproduction before changing code.

## Risks and rollback

Enabling interpolation alone can make render-written bones jitter more severely.
Clock refactoring can accidentally extend injury payout windows or shorten fuses.
Keep scoring time domains explicit and compare event ledgers rather than totals alone.
If automatic bone interpolation fails, retain physics interpolation for bodies and use
one render-only skin path based on interpolated body transforms.
Rollback only the failing presentation strategy, not explicit timestamps or clock separation.
Do not mask a failure by increasing physics TPS or weakening an error detector.

## Done and handoff evidence

Attach clock traces, ownership table, reset tests, and the exact Godot version.
Document the remaining native smoothness gate for R14.
No unexpected script errors or interpolation warnings remain in headless affected suites.
R04/R08 receive simulation support/pose ownership; R07 receives presentation camera time.
R06 receives timestamp semantics; R09 receives separate settlement deadlines.
R11 receives explicit phase/pause/replay timing for audio envelopes.
Close this task only after the implemented interface and focused tests exist.
close_reason: Monotonic wall clock40 and integrated clock10, skin210 actual weighted-vertex seam pass; simulation/render ownership and interpolation resets integrated. Evidence docs/repair/evidence/R05.md; physical rig issue remains R08, native smoothness R14.

# R06 — Replay timestamped immutable actor and camera state

Priority: P1. Prerequisites: R05, R07, R08, R09. Unblocks: R11, R12.
Workspace: `/Users/tyler/Documents/GitHub/stair-dismount`; Godot 4.7.2 Compatibility.
This card repairs faithful playback after clock, camera, rig and settlement contracts land.
Reserve the shared main/rider/traffic writer slots; do not edit those files concurrently.
Read new AGENTS.md instructions and the completed prerequisites' handoffs before implementation.
R01 infrastructure is a transitive prerequisite through R05; its fixture/runner handoff must exist.

## Background and measured failure

`main.gd` records rigid-body transforms during CRASH and plays them back after RESULTS.
The campaign banks route-best improvements once; replay must never create another claim.
F05: actual C dispatch changes `camera_style` but recorded transforms overwrite the view.
F06: snapshots omit FOV, so replay retains the results lens instead of the recorded lens.
F07: the recorder discards remainder and playback assumes every sample is .05 s apart.
At .55 with 90 Hz physics, measured samples were .055,.110,.165,.220 simulated seconds.
At .25 the spacing was .052778; at .18 it was .050, yet playback uses the same .05 divisor.
Sources: `main.gd:327-342,451-485,487-533,580`; `game_hud.gd:397-398` promises C camera.
Evidence: `builds/repair_audit/state_ui_probe.*`, `camera_clock_probe.*`, audit UI-04/05/06.
The `.gd` probes use real dispatcher/physics fixtures and separately identify constructed clocks.
Final injury and traffic restoration already exists at `main.gd:507-514`; preserve that behavior.
`traffic_car.gd:241-248` currently applies snapshots by mutating live driver/armed/cause/damage fields.
That live mutation is incompatible with the shared immutable-presentation replay contract.

## Timeline contract and rationale

Create one immutable attempt tape keyed by stable actor ID, never incidental array index.
Physics actor samples carry actual elapsed simulation time from R05, sorted monotonically.
Capture a complete initial crash state at bail and an exact final settlement state from R09.
Preserve an irregular final interval instead of treating it as another full .05-second period.
Retain accumulator remainder for capture scheduling; interpolation uses stored timestamps.
Stable IDs and recorded presence permit playback of actors cleaned up before settlement.
Keep bounded replay resources until tape discard or rebuild visual proxies from actor metadata.
Do not retain an unbounded scene history or create a second physical simulation.
Live camera sampling has per-render ownership because R05/R07 move the camera on render time.
Record camera transform, FOV and sample simulation time after the final safe render camera update.
Record initial/final camera boundaries even when no render sample occurred at that physics instant.
Use the latest completed render sample at each boundary and record its own time/age explicitly.
Do not pair a stale camera with new actor state and label both as sampled simultaneously.
Camera samples interpolate on their own sorted timestamps against the same playback clock.
Use bail as tape simulation origin0. Normalize source camera times to that origin and preserve
pre-bail age; never relabel a stale source as simultaneous with an actor boundary. Store increasing
capture sequence; at equal timestamps the latest sequence wins before bracketing distinct times.
Outside the camera sample range hold earliest/latest views, including an older final render source.
Actor time clamps to [0,duration]. A zero-duration tape disables replay; no interpolation divides by0.
The default view reproduces the recorded camera; C cycles recorded → chase → side → overhead.
Alternate views use replayed actor focus and R07 safety, never the frozen final live torso.
This keeps the promised camera choice useful without adding forces, driver logic or payout.

## Data and ownership interfaces

Tape header: attempt ID, route/pose identity, duration, capture cadence and stable actor catalog.
Actor catalog: ID, visual resource/kind, spawn transform and presentation reconstruction metadata.
Include immutable camera-query shape geometry/local transforms for dynamic props in the catalog.
Actor samples: simulation time, ID→transform, presence/visibility and discrete visual states.
Record limb severity, prop damage, traffic wheel/lamp/driver display and fuse visual state.
Record receipts and event visibility with explicit simulation timestamps and stable event IDs.
Camera samples: simulation time, camera transform, FOV and explicit boundary/sample provenance.
Avoid storing mutable live dictionaries by reference; deep-copy/finalize the tape at settlement.
Immutable means playback cannot write to tape entries or authoritative live state.
Replay owns presentation proxies or equivalent isolated visual state, with physics disabled.
Alternate cameras query route geometry plus query-only prop geometry at replay time, excluding frozen
live dynamic RIDs. A bounded static query proxy set uses numeric collision_layer 0x10
(Godot inspector layer 5), collision_mask 0. Existing live masks 3 and 7 ignore that bit;
replay queries combine static bit 1 and proxy bit 0x10 as numeric collision mask 0x11.
Never attach contact/driver/payout callbacks to query proxies; synchronize them before camera solving.
Dispose query proxies on every exit. Test a prop with disjoint early/final transforms: only the
visible replay-time hull can obstruct an alternate view, not its invisible frozen final collider.
It must not call hit/ignite/shatter/activate, driver integration, impulse or bank APIs.
Never use live `apply_snapshot` to modify cause/armed/fuse/paid fields during playback.
Use a dedicated visual snapshot adapter for proxies; keep authoritative settlement state intact.
Isolate mutable material/morph/wheel state as well as dictionaries. Test live shader/damage values
during proxy playback; sharing mutable resources cannot satisfy presentation isolation.
Hide live meshes/effects while proxies are visible without disabling needed result state ownership.
On entry preserve final live presentation visibility and camera state for exact restoration.
On completion, retry, route exit or disposal, remove proxies and restore the agreed final state.
Pause/help stop the playback clock using R05's pause baseline; closing returns to the same sample.
R11 consumes replay entry/exit lifecycle hooks for music-only playback; do not synthesize live claims/sounds.
R10 continues to own funding/save UI, so playback never changes durable/session funding status.

## Implementation steps

1. Inspect R05 clock/interpolation APIs, R07 camera API, R08 skin ownership and R09 finalization.
2. Capture current failures with R01's isolated fixture and preserve the evidence JSON/logs.
3. Introduce typed/documented tape records and stable actor IDs through the existing builders.
4. Capture initial/final actor state and timestamped event/discrete visual state at simulation boundaries.
5. Capture the finalized live camera once per render update with transform/FOV and sample time.
6. Freeze/deep-copy the completed tape; validate sorting, ID resolution and duration once on entry.
7. Build bounded nonphysical replay visuals and suppress inappropriate residual live effects.
8. Implement timestamp bracketing and independent actor/camera interpolation with endpoint handling.
9. Apply discrete states/events only at their recorded times; no interpolation of damage/payment.
10. Implement the four-view C cycle through R07 using interpolated replay actor focus.
11. Restore/dispose replay presentation on every exit, including help/pause/retry during playback.
12. Extend replay tests and publish music-only lifecycle hooks and visible event contracts for R11/R12.

## Independent acceptance and commands

Use R01 pre-_ready isolated fixtures, absolute logs and bounded per-process test deadlines.
Run targeted `tests/test_replay.gd` with `/opt/homebrew/bin/godot --headless --fixed-fps 60`.
Use R01's fixture argument and log under `/Users/tyler/Documents/GitHub/stair-dismount/builds/repair/R06/`.
Then run `GODOT_BIN=/opt/homebrew/bin/godot ./tools/test.sh` through the bounded runner.
Use an independently timed constant-velocity actor to select sample/interpolation expectations.
At selected timestamps, position error must be ≤.002 m for this linear fixture.
Choose endpoints and values between irregular samples without computing expected index via production.
Cover .55/.25/.18 segments, time-rate switches, multiple render rates and a shortened final interval.
Tape duration must match independent elapsed simulation time within the actual sampled physics delta.
Use logged deltas at the time rate rather than assuming every tick is 1/90 of a simulation second.
Test initial/final snapshots, deleted actors, visibility changes and identical timestamps at boundaries.
Use distinct camera transforms at one timestamp, an older final render sample, and zero-duration
tape controls to verify deterministic tie, hold, and disabled-playback rules independently.
Projection fixture uses nondefault FOV and known world points; screen error must be ≤1 design pixel.
At one fixed playback timestamp C must cycle four views and return to recorded on the fourth press.
Compare actor transforms and independent projection while changing view; no timeline/state drift.
Capture the authoritative live state before replay and compare it during and after two playbacks.
Include scores, fund/save status, boosts, cause/armed/fuse/paid, transforms and velocities.
Require exact accounting/discrete-state equality and ≤.00001 transform component drift while frozen.
Replay must not call payout/impulse callbacks; observe actual callback counts, not a fake rules mock.
Test pause/help at mid-replay, complete return, retry, route selection and short/two-frame tapes.
Test unbroken props, evolving all-eleven injury states, traffic wheels/lights and fused/exploded drums.
Record tape/proxy counts before and after repeated attempts; disposed proxies must not accumulate.
Native R14 must inspect motion/framing/effect correspondence; headless projections are not screenshots.

## Risks, rollback and completion evidence

The largest risk is accidental authoritative mutation hidden inside reusable visual snapshot methods.
Audit adapters and use pre/during/post state comparison to expose cause/fuse/driver pollution.
Camera render timestamps can lag physics; preserve sample provenance instead of falsifying a boundary.
Limit tape/proxy lifetime to one completed attempt and release it on route/attempt replacement.
Rollback the replay integration from the preserved snapshot without deleting a player's saved records.
Done requires immutable tape/schema notes, independent timing/projection/state logs and lifecycle checks.
Attach commands, fixtures, changed-file list and measured memory/proxy counts, not only assertion totals.
Keep native audiovisual acceptance pending for R14 while providing R11's entry/exit hooks.
R11 can then implement sound transitions; R12 can stress the complete faithful three-route loop.

# R07 — Keep the actual camera outside geometry and correctly aimed

Priority: P1. Prerequisites: R05, R04. Unblocks: R06, R12.
Workspace: `/Users/tyler/Documents/GitHub/stair-dismount`; Godot 4.7.2 Compatibility.
This task repairs camera geometry/order using completed clock and riding support contracts.
Reserve `main.gd` and camera-policy file ownership before editing; no concurrent shared writers.
Read newly added AGENTS.md plus R05/R04 completion evidence before implementation.

## Background, evidence and limits

The default crash camera uses `scripts/crash_camera.gd` to pick a clear desired position.
`scripts/main.gd:540-582` then smooths camera position/target, adds shake, aims and clamps height.
F08: a candidate lens inside a real world collider is accepted as clear by the policy.
`crash_camera.gd:8-14` creates a ray with default `hit_from_inside=false`.
`crash_camera.gd:20` accepts the candidate immediately if that ray has no reported hit.
The probe placed a real StaticBody3D box around `(5.8,3.4,-6.8)`, outside the rider target.
Production clear_view returned true and the chooser retained the position inside that solid.
An independently configured inside-aware ray reported a collision at the lens origin.
F09: `main.gd:579` aims before `:581-582` changes lens height to satisfy the floor constraint.
A deliberately below-floor starting camera produced a 71.643° final aiming error.
That large error is a constructed condition, not a native run observation.
Evidence: `builds/repair_audit/camera_clock_probe.gd`, its JSON/log and audit UI-03/UI-07.
Reproduce it headlessly after real physics frames; do not turn Blender images into native evidence.
Normal-play frequency and smooth-path occlusion remain observation gates in this task.

## Chosen safety contract and rationale

Validate the actual displayed camera lens, not only a distant desired endpoint.
Use current real world/prop CollisionShape3D geometry on collision mask 3, excluding rider layer 4.
Do not use nominal prop radius, authored mesh appearance or the camera helper as its own oracle.
Check initial overlap separately, since ray/sweep behavior can ignore an intersecting origin.
Use a small lens-volume shape query, initially a sphere radius .18 m, as an explicit safety margin.
Treat .18 as a camera collision envelope, not a promise that every near-plane corner is covered.
Measure near-plane corner clipping in R14 before enlarging this margin or changing projection.
Generate a bounded candidate set near the intended chase/side/overhead composition.
Prefer same-side raises/shifts before mirroring so the rider's screen direction stays readable.
Then test the smoothed/interpolated travel path and final lens against actual solid geometry.
If a path is blocked, shorten it to a safe point or choose a verified alternate, not a blind lerp.
Apply floor, overlap and path corrections before calculating final look_at orientation.
Apply bounded shake to the target, preserving lens safety; shake must not move the lens into solids.
Keep existing chase scale and visible traffic handoff; do not solve obstruction by zooming away.
When no candidate is safe, keep a verified last-safe position or use a documented bounded fallback.
Revalidate last-safe against moving props; stale safety is not a perpetual exemption.
Avoid cycling endlessly among candidates or feeding camera placement back into physics bodies.

## Presentation API and prerequisite handoff

Consume R05's render clock/interpolated focus and reset behavior, not raw frame-scale division.
Consume R04's actual support/tread contract when applying the floor-height bound.
Keep the production camera transform owned by one render update after physics presentation sampling.
Expose a camera update API taking phase/view mode, focus, presentation delta and world-query context.
Return final transform/FOV plus optional diagnostic reason for candidate/path/floor changes.
R06 will reuse that API with replay proxy focus for chase/side/overhead views.
Recorded replay mode will restore timestamped recorded transform/FOV without another live camera solve.

Idle settlement means the causally relevant action has genuinely become quiet for the declared dwell.

1. Read the R02 save-result and campaign-state contract; avoid recomputing banked totals in HUD.

and leave the viewport case explicitly unresolved for R14.

Recovery choices use actual HUD signals and existing modal ownership, not a second modal state machine or a developer approval prompt. HELP restores a valid recovery control; completion restores ordinary visible focus. The visible phase controls and save action have explicit cyclic Tab/Shift-Tab order.

The R06 replay HUD reads injury severities from `replay_sample.limbs`, never the live ragdoll. It also accepts pure historical receipt presentation in REPLAY with a `RECORDED RECEIPTS` heading; main owns immutable event timing and must not score or play receipt audio during playback.

The new status panel occupies unused MENU/READY center-right space and sits to the right of the RESULTS report; it does not cover the injury ledger, claim amount, primary run/replay actions, or breaker control. Long receipts deliberately abbreviate the name with an ellipsis while retaining the complete dollar amount. Long titles have explicit ellipsis behavior. The live payout font is 38 logical pixels so $999,999,999 fits without reducing essential text to a tiny size.

The production minimum window is explicitly 960×600. The logical canvas remains 1440×900 with Godot's existing `canvas_items` / `keep` letterbox behavior. The headless test sets each requested raw window size, retains the actual root window size, records its visible logical rectangle and canvas transform, and checks actual visible actionable controls for bounds and overlap. Every retained case reported the 1440×900 logical canvas.

Each window was inspected in MENU, READY, CRASH, RESULTS, HELP, and PAUSE: 30 retained snapshots in `records_ui_report.json`. Font metrics include amounts up to 999999999, three-route totals up to 2999999997, all eleven fractured injury rows, wrapped recovery copy, and a long receipt. Modal-covered controls are excluded from the actionable overlap set using main's real ownership policy.

Commands use `/opt/homebrew/bin/godot --headless --path /Users/tyler/Documents/GitHub/stair-dismount --fixed-fps 60 --script res://tests/<suite>.gd --log-file <case>/engine.log -- --test-mode --records-path=<case>/records.json`, bounded by `tools/run_bounded.py --timeout-seconds 180` with the exact summary. description:
# R11 — Verify audio transitions during pause and replay

Priority: P2.
Depends on: R03, R05, R06.
Unblocks: R12.

## Context for a fresh implementer

Workspace: `/Users/tyler/Documents/GitHub/stair-dismount`.
The Godot 4.7.2 Compatibility game has three skateboard crash routes.
A finite moving traffic encounter follows the descent and one crashbreaker extends it.
The treatment fund is scored from actual contacts; sounds must never produce game events.
Fifteen original audio files and a pooled sound director already exist.
The engine/rolling loops, music, and receipt/impact sounds live in scripts/sound_director.gd.
Main owns phase and calls the sound update functions.
No project AGENTS.md or Git repository existed when planning; check any new instructions.
Reserve shared source files and use R01 isolated fixtures.
R03 specifies modal/focus state; R05 specifies time domains; R06 specifies replay events.

## Investigation rather than invented defect

`main.gd:501–526` returns from replay before updating rolling and traffic loops.
`main.gd:532–533` updates those loops only outside the replay branch.
This makes stale loop state plausible, particularly entering replay immediately after settlement.
Actual unwanted native audio has not been demonstrated.
Headless mode deliberately avoids native AudioStreamPlayer allocation in the sound director.
A test that checks zero players in headless mode cannot prove normal playback correctness.
Attempt source-process playback in isolated storage before editing. Separate native player-state
observations from listening. If native allocation is unavailable, change only independently
reproduced behavior and publish every unobserved native case as a mandatory R14 gate.

Why: sound communicates launch, injury, cascade handoffs, and claim settlement.
Lingering engines or repeated receipts can make frozen replay/results feel broken.
The repair scope is coherent playback state, not new composition or a large mixer framework.

## Chosen state policy

Keep the fifteen existing assets unless inspection finds clipping or a broken resource.
Maintain separate policies for music, continuous action loops, and event one-shots.
Music may continue through pause/help at the existing intended level.
Rolling and driver-engine loops stop or fade promptly on RESULTS, MENU, and REPLAY.
Paused gameplay loops pause coherently and resume without replaying old one-shots.
Mute affects every bus/player including currently playing pooled effects.
A muted preference applies immediately and remains session-active if persistence fails.
Focus loss uses the R03 pause policy; do not continue action audio while gameplay is suspended.
Replay uses music only in this repair; stop live action audio at entry and do not add an event track.
Visible receipts/events remain in R06; playback cannot call live scoring or sound callbacks.
A later replay event track would need its own recorded sound/pitch/gain schema and isolated cooldowns.
No deferred replay effect can play after playback returns to results.

## Timing and resource contract

Loop envelope duration uses active presentation time from R05.
Do not calculate envelope increments from a newly changed Engine.time_scale.
Stream pitch changes stay bounded and must not use a zero or negative pitch.
Use the existing pool or a small bounded pool; no player is allocated per physics contact.
Stop and detach streams during sound director teardown.
Retrying/changing routes does not leave a previous director or loop alive.
An exported app must load audio through ResourceLoader rather than assuming source WAV paths.
Native audio device failure is a recoverable lack of playback, not a game crash.
Report backend failure separately from a gameplay transition defect.

## Implementation sequence

1. Inspect current sound allocation, bus levels, pause modes, and teardown.
2. Launch an audio-enabled diagnostic in an isolated candidate/source sandbox.
3. Exercise immediate results-to-replay and observe actual loop state and audible behavior.
4. Log live loop playing/paused/volume states with phase transitions.
5. If a case fails, add one explicit phase transition method to the existing sound director.
6. Have main notify that method on launch, pause, replay, settlement, route change, and focus loss.
7. Enter/exit music-only replay explicitly without consuming live sound cooldowns or event callbacks.
8. Verify mute applies consistently to all allocated players and newly requested sounds.
9. Run the focused native state test, audio resource tests, and route-teardown test.
10. Hand audible quality/mix observations to R14 for final native validation.

## Independent acceptance cases

- Enter RUN, verify rolling sound starts at an eligible speed and stops after settlement.
- Enter RESULTS and immediately REPLAY; no live rolling/traffic engine remains audible.
- Pause during a cascade; no new impact/receipt one-shot is triggered while paused.
- Resume once; paused sounds do not restart as a burst of old events.
- Toggle mute during a long effect and during a loop; both stop audibly or mute via bus.
- Request a new effect while muted; it remains inaudible.
- Repeat retry and route replacement twenty times; allocated player count remains bounded.
- Play replay twice; music-only policy persists and no live impact/receipt/engine sounds fire.
- Exit replay early; no stale action sound can resume after results return.
- Verify invalid/empty audio resources fail cleanly without a game SCRIPT ERROR.
- Inspect audio files for nonempty length, finite samples, and peak clipping.
- Publish the source audio inventory for R13 to verify the exported candidate; no candidate blocks R11.

Native allocation/state tests are separate from listening evidence.
Waveform/peak checks can prove file properties but do not prove pleasant mixing.
Headless resource checks remain useful and should not be removed.
Do not insert fabricated sound-player mocks that merely mirror the phase method.
If the environment cannot open audio, record the exact backend limitation and leave native
acceptance pending rather than asserting the sound experience is verified.

## Risks and fallback

Pooled effects may still be playing when mute or replay starts; inspect every active player.
Repeated phase callbacks must not queue another finish/receipt sound.
Music-only replay is chosen to avoid an unnecessary event-track feature and live cooldown coupling.
Do not tie a live engine loop to a wreck that is UNCONTROLLED or SETTLED.
Changing sound pool lifetime can cause orphan warnings at exit; preserve explicit teardown.
Prefer a measured small transition fix over replacing the audio engine.
If the baseline transition works, keep it and attach the observation as a completed investigation.

## Done and handoff evidence

Record whether each initial hypothesis failed or passed and why an edit was necessary.
Attach transition state logs, asset checks, native listening notes if available, and engine version.
List which checks require audio hardware and remain for R14.
R12 receives a bounded route/replay/paused teardown scenario.
No payout or force code changes are justified by an audio observation.
Close the source investigation after resource/lifecycle checks and supported fixes, with pass/fail/unobserved cases.
Unobserved native cases block R14/R15, not construction of the candidate in R13.
A native failure reopens R11 and requires a new candidate through R13.
