# R12 — Integrate and stress the complete three-route loop

Priority: P1.
Depends on: R02, R03, R04, R06, R07, R08, R09, R10, R11.
Unblocks: R13.

## Context for a fresh implementer

Workspace: `/Users/tyler/Documents/GitHub/stair-dismount`.
Target is Godot 4.7.2, 90 Hz physics, Compatibility rendering.
The game has Civic Cascade, Night Market, and Port Authority routes.
Players charge, push on the run-up, steer, bail, spend one crashbreaker, settle, replay, and retry.
Eleven articulated body regions show damage; the separate board cannot earn injury payout.
The fictional insurance campaign banks the best claim per route toward 600000.
Upstream tasks repaired saves, input, skating, clocks, replay, camera, skin, traffic, UI, and audio.
No project AGENTS.md or Git repository existed at planning time; check new instructions.
Reserve shared files and use the isolated pre-ready fixture contract from R01.
This task integrates existing fixes and fills actual seam regressions rather than adding features.

## Why an integration gate is necessary

Individual passing suites can miss interactions such as focused help during a failed-save replay.
The original tests passed accounting and controlled collisions while real input and skating failed.
Test cases must use actual viewport dispatch and Godot bodies at the relevant seam.
R01's preserved failing reproductions must now pass their repaired acceptance conditions.
Do not replace those probes with calls to the new production helper as their own oracle.
Only add cases when they verify a distinct risk or confirmed bug.
A high assertion count, score, or object cascade is not an objective proof of fun.
The practical goal here is predictable choices, visible consequences, reliable retry, and stable play.

## Integration contract

Retain all three existing routes, hats, poses, injury thresholds, and one crashbreaker charge.
The default first-launch line still demonstrates a physically caused cascade.
Alternative lanes/poses/charge/early versus late breaker can change actual outcomes.
Never award fallback points or force a wreck to meet a gameplay test score.
Every payout has a traceable accepted injury/contact event and capped object identity.
A single object and each finite anatomical budget cannot pay twice via replay/retry artifacts.
An unarmed background vehicle collision cannot fund the player.
Committed treatment money equals the sum of persisted route bests.
Pending session bests remain separate and do not display as secured.
Replay cannot change score, committed records, live fuses, forces, or causal edge ledger.
The supported result exits, route changes, and quit paths stop all simulation ownership cleanly.

## Bounded scenario matrix

Run one ordinary launch on each route with the recommended lane, default pose, and .75 charge.
Run one full-charge outer-lane descent on each route, with and without a real push cadence.
Run controlled no-bail-before-end cases to expose ground support drift.
Run one real taxi near miss and one genuine taxi strike at supported maximum speed.
Run one early breaker, one late breaker, and a repeated-held breaker input sequence.
Run a car-A-to-B-to-C case through actual body contact, with an unarmed negative control.
Run a spinning wreck/fuse-pending settlement case and the explicit early Enter filing path.
Run modal help/pause/focus-loss transitions from READY, RUN, CRASH, and REPLAY.
Run blocked saving, successful Retry Save, weaker retry, and restart recovery.
Run exact replay start, mid-damage sample, C camera changes, end, and early exit.
Run twenty route/retry replacements alternating routes to inspect resource lifetime.
Use a fixed small set of three seeds for contact jitter variation; log them explicitly.
Do not multiply every dimension into thousands of redundant simulations.

## Implementation sequence

1. Confirm each prerequisite's actual acceptance artifacts and installed interface.
2. Run preserved audit probes before adding any new integration fixture.
3. Compare route ground height/contact data with independent world geometry queries.
4. Drive real key and GUI events rather than calling launch/retry handlers for focus cases.
5. Capture score/event/actor state at settlement and before/after replay.
6. Reopen save files independently and restart a new scene to verify persistence.
7. Exercise body teardown and scan process logs for unexpected errors or orphan warnings.
8. Add only missing seam tests and fix minimal integration inconsistencies they expose.
9. Run the full bounded suite once after those fixes; repeat only affected failures afterward.
10. Record per-scenario evidence and send the passing source identity to R13.

## Quantitative acceptance oracles

- Taxi near miss retains positive independent hull clearance and never activates the taxi.
- Grounded outer descents meet R04 wheel-support and penetration tolerances.
- Camera lens/frustum checks satisfy R07 in all chosen modes and constructed overlap cases.
- Skin follows its intended simulated/interpolated bones within R08 tolerance.
- Each attempt consumes at most one breaker and preserves its bounded impulse budget.
- Settlement reports quiet, manual, simulation-cap, or presentation-cap truthfully.
- A spinning hazardous actor cannot satisfy the quiet criterion.
- Records never partially apply invalid fields or overwrite unsupported future bytes.
- A failed save never updates committed money or emits a newly funded ending.
- A retry commit and repeated retry do not duplicate its improvement.
- Replay samples at timestamps match stored transform/FOV/discrete state within R06 tolerances.
- Live state/score/event hashes remain unchanged by replay presentation.
- Root actor/player counts return to a stable range after queued frees complete.
- Unexpected SCRIPT ERROR, engine ERROR, leaked resource, and orphan diagnostics are zero.
- Every process finishes within R01's explicit per-suite deadline.

Numerical tolerances belong to their upstream physical contract, not an arbitrary score threshold.
If a case legitimately changes after real collision repair, update the scenario expectation from
independent evidence and explain the change; do not weaken the collision oracle.
All traces include source/build identity, route, seed, pose, controls, time rate, and engine version.

## Gameplay attainability and observation

Measure that a normal player-visible control sequence can cause the intended domino cascade.
Measure the selected one-breaker landing choices and their different physical/event outcomes.
Verify the 600000 campaign remains attainable through legitimate capped events across routes.
Use a reproducible good-play input trace, not invisible impulses or direct money mutation.
If a fix makes attainable scores materially different, inspect actual route balance and declare
that follow-up separately; do not move caps or inject awards just to preserve an old benchmark.
Native manual play in R14 checks whether feedback remains understandable and responsive.
Player enjoyment requires actual players; mark it unmeasured unless observations are collected.

## Risks and failure handling

Logical prerequisites can be done while their edits conflict in main.gd; inspect the integrated source.
An isolated runner can still read a shared file if startup overrides the fixture; verify path traces.
Physics outcomes have small solver variance; assert meaningful inequalities and causal events,
not exact bitwise contact counts or one lucky payout.
Do not suppress engine errors because a test also printed PASS.
If a failure belongs to a prerequisite contract, reopen that task with the failing evidence.
Keep unrelated gameplay tuning and art regeneration out of this integration gate.

## Done and handoff evidence

Attach the bounded scenario table with pass/fail and artifact paths.
Attach independent state/record comparisons, resource counts, and full-suite exit status.
Record unresolved native visual/audio/focus cases explicitly for R14.
R13 receives one stable source/assets manifest to export.
No candidate package or final release is claimed by completion of this source-only gate.
Close only when the integrated source passes all required automated regressions.

Use `br --db /Users/tyler/Documents/GitHub/stair-dismount/.beads/beads.db` and claim R13.

STAIR // WRECK is a three-route skateboard/ragdoll/traffic game with local treatment-fund records.

Define build ID as a digest of canonical runtime/packaging inputs and engine identity, with schema version.
Use a separate run ID for timestamps/logs so output hashes do not form a circular build-ID dependency.

Preserve relative resource paths and import settings; do not silently export whatever an old cache contains.
If staging regenerates import metadata, verify it represents the original authored inputs/settings.
Store immutable build identity in app Resources and an Info.plist build-ID field before signing.
Keep output hashes in an external manifest so hashing the manifest itself cannot be circular.
Manifest fields include schema, build/run IDs, input inventory/digest, engine identity, plist, app file map,
PCK hash/size, ZIP hash/size, bounded-check results, extraction path, and candidate status.

## Candidate construction contract

Write a new directory `builds/candidates/<build-id>-<run-id>/` and refuse to reuse a nonempty one.

Keep the declared minimum macOS version consistent with both runtime slices and the app metadata.
Verify local engine version matches the tested R12 engine; a change requires renewed integration evidence.
Run import/export with bounded deadlines and the R01 error policy, including script/engine diagnostics.
Copy the actual executable, PCK, icon, and both license notices into the candidate bundle.
Validate plist executable/name/version/build ID and executable mode before signing.
Apply/verify the ad-hoc signature only after all bundle modifications are complete.
Build the ZIP from that signed candidate; do not append files afterward or sign a different directory.
Treat export/copy/sign/archive failure as a failed candidate, preserving diagnostic logs.
No final version bump is required merely to repair provenance; record the candidate build ID unambiguously.

## Extracted archive verification contract

Verify ZIP CRC and exact app-member inventory; reject traversal/absolute paths or escaping symlinks.
Allow documented macOS archive metadata only; do not mistake it for unexpected runtime app contents.
Extract with the intended macOS tool into a fresh writable directory, including paths with spaces.

Verify the extracted signature, plist, build identity, runtime architectures, PCK digest, and licenses.
Do not hardcode seven files: a new build-identity resource legitimately changes the member count.
Run the extracted executable from an unrelated empty working directory with no source project mounted as res://.
Complete all three packaged `--self-check --level=0/1/2` routes using bounded process invocations.
Require each expected level's completion/positive score/wreck evidence and reject unexpected diagnostics.
Run the existing source-side assets probe against that runtime/PCK; label it as an external probe.

Check representative docs/tests/tools/Blender exclusions and enumerate PCK entries if supported locally.
Ensure new repair evidence, test fixtures, `.beads`, and candidate directories are excluded from the PCK.
No probe may read missing runtime resources from the source tree and thereby hide an incomplete export.

## Normal packaged persistence acceptance

Use R01 `--records-path=<absolute isolated file>` without `--test-mode` or `--self-check` for storage proof.
Normal presentation/storage selection is distinct from automation; this override never selects the real profile.
Exercise the packaged record service/scene with a controlled claim and preferences, then quit/relaunch.

Use a missing/unwritable isolated destination and verify R02's pending claim and truthful non-secured state.
Resolve storage, retry once, relaunch, and prove a single committed contribution, not additive retry credit.
The bookkeeping fixture validates packaged persistence wiring, not the provenance of a physical crash.
R14 additionally earns a real claim through native play and checks normal restart persistence.
Keep all fixture/profile paths inside the candidate check directory; never inspect the actual user's records.

## Negative controls and acceptance evidence

Run verifier fixtures for corrupt ZIP, stale ZIP/app mismatch, missing runtime member, bad plist/build ID,
single-architecture engine, altered PCK, source mutation during construction, and timed-out packaged process.
Each fixture must fail the relevant gate; do not mutate the preserved baseline or accepted candidate in place.

Provide R14 a ready-to-open extracted app and the exact ZIP SHA/build ID to record with observations.
Do not substitute Blender reconstructions, headless scores, or asset counts for R14 native player evidence.

## Completion and final handoff

Close R13 only when candidate construction, exact extracted-byte verification, packaged routes/resources,
normal isolated persistence, and negative verifier controls all pass with actual recorded outputs.

Unblocks: R15.

## Context for a fresh implementer

Workspace: `/Users/tyler/Documents/GitHub/stair-dismount`.
The repaired game targets Godot 4.7.2 Compatibility on macOS 11 or newer.
It ships three skateboard stair-crash routes, articulated damage, hats, traffic, and one breaker.
Its campaign banks best route claims to fund Mom's treatment in the fictional story.
R13 provides an identifiable candidate ZIP extracted into a clean validation directory.
R12 has checked isolated automated correctness; native visual and audible quality remain separate.
No project AGENTS.md or Git repository existed when planning; inspect any added instructions.
Use a disposable save directory provided before startup, never the player's existing records.
Record the actual machine, renderer, window size, scale factor, engine and candidate build ID.

## Why headless and Blender evidence are insufficient

The original deliverable had Blender renders of actual runtime geometry and HUD rectangles.
Those renders cannot demonstrate Godot skin shaders, camera motion, text rendering, or frame pacing.
Headless focus probes establish specific dispatcher defects but cannot prove all native controls.
Waveform checks cannot prove correct native output or a coherent sound mix.
This task directly observes the extracted candidate app a player would launch.
Do not substitute source execution for candidate execution in the release evidence.
Use source execution only to isolate a candidate-only discrepancy.

## Evidence capture policy

Prefer actual native app screenshots or Godot viewport captures from a displayed process.
Label every image with build ID, route, phase, time rate, and native versus fallback provenance.
Capture short native screen recordings for movement/camera/interpolation judgments.
Still screenshots alone cannot establish smoothness or prevent a transient clipping event.
Use available computer-use tools through their documented entry points.
Do not assume a visible surface exists or fabricate screenshots if native services fail.
A renderer/device/window failure leaves the corresponding acceptance case pending.
Record the exact error and any safe diagnostic tried; no task may pretend that gate passed.
A Blender MCP render can supplement an asset investigation but does not complete this task.
No external messages or model invocations are required for the native check.

## Native route walkthrough

For each route, open the extracted app in a new isolated record fixture.
Verify the candidate build identity and the displayed first-run fund state.
Select all three poses and hats and observe readable continuous body/board silhouettes.
Charge, push, and steer the recommended line with real keyboard input.
Observe wheel support down the stairs at ordinary and maximum attainable speed.
Make a deliberate taxi near miss and a separate genuine obstacle strike.
Observe bail continuity, visible limb damage, and body articulation on treads.
Use the one breaker early and late across two attempts; inspect its preview and actual impulse.
Follow the physical traffic handoff at the road without an abrupt occluded camera jump.
Wait for quiet settlement in one attempt and explicitly file with Enter in another.
Watch replay in recorded, chase, side, and overhead view, then retry and change route.
Close and restart the candidate with the same isolated fixture to verify records persist.

## Required interaction matrix

Open help over a focused MENU button and press Enter: the route must not start underneath it.
Open help/pause over a focused READY pose button and press Enter: the pose must not change.
Close the modal and verify valid restored focus and intended keyboard navigation.
Hold Tab after clicking a non-modal button in RUN: held slow motion works consistently.
Lose window focus while charging; return and release Space: no surprise launch.
Lose focus while steering/slow/aftertouch; return with released keys: no stuck action.
Pause/help in RUN, CRASH, and REPLAY; verify frozen simulation and coherent resume.
Mute during a traffic loop and an impact sound; both are inaudible afterward.
Return RESULTS→REPLAY immediately; no stale live wheel or engine loop remains.
Use keyboard and mouse for Retry Save in an intentionally blocked fixture.
Verify pending versus committed funding wording and restart survival after a successful retry.

## Motion, rendering, and UI observations

Observe live and replay at time rates 1, .55, .25, and .18.
Inspect at default 1280×800 and the declared minimum window from R10.
Also inspect 1024×768, 1920×1080, and the available high-DPI native scale.
Record unsupported cases honestly; do not claim a scale factor that was not tested.
Watch the actual smoothed camera and near-plane, not merely the candidate position.
Inspect skin joints, torso/limb overlap, hats, damage highlights, and board contact shadows.
Check receipts, insurance values, injury labels, and result controls for readability.
Save native screenshots of menu, riding, impact, traffic, results, replay, and save warning.
Verify no viewport has clipped primary actions or text under an overlay.
Record a frame-time trace after warm-up on the actual machine.
Compare with an equivalent source baseline when available; flag a >10% regression in
median or p95 active-play frame time for investigation rather than inventing a speed promise.
Frame pacing must show no unexplained periodic stall associated with replay/skin updates.
The 10% threshold is an investigation trigger, not measured performance claimed by the plan.

## Independent pass criteria

All three native walkthroughs finish without a script/engine error or control dead end.
Wheel support and camera observations agree with upstream quantitative bounds.
Modal keyboard actions do not affect underlying gameplay.
There is no unexpected route/reset interpolation streak or persistent visible skin detachment.
Replay explains the same event order/damage and all four camera choices visibly differ.
Action audio follows the selected R11 policy and native mute works for every category.
Committed records survive a candidate restart; failed saving is plainly pending.
Native menu/results/help remain legible at every declared supported size actually tested.
Capture evidence from the extracted candidate, including its manifest identity.
A reviewer can connect observations to the input sequence and exact artifact tested.

This is stability/feedback validation, not a claim that the game is objectively fun.
If a real playtest participant is available, record their observed confusion/retry intent
without turning subjective notes into fabricated statistics or an enjoyment guarantee.
No human-response survey or new analytics service is required to close stability cases.

## Failure handling and rerun scope

For each failure attach route/pose/control trace and a native recording or screenshot.
Identify whether the cause belongs to source logic, exporter/package, renderer, or device.
Reopen the owning repair task instead of lowering its acceptance requirement.
Any source or asset fix invalidates the candidate identity and requires a new R13 candidate.
Rerun affected native cases plus launch/replay/save smoke checks on all three routes.
Do not reuse screenshots from a replaced build as evidence for the new package.
If native execution is unavailable, retain candidate and explicit pending checklist;
R15 promotion stays blocked by this task, while independent source repairs remain completed.

## Done and handoff evidence

Create a native validation report with scenario results, environment, and artifact hashes.
Store screenshots/recordings with honest provenance in a candidate-specific evidence directory.
Include native log scan, frame-time observations, listening notes, and restart file checks.
Mark any unsupported environment limitation rather than claiming universal portability.
R15 receives the exact candidate ID and approval-by-evidence for final promotion.
Close only when required native evidence exists and every mandatory case passes.

# R15 — Promote the verified game and repair launcher provenance

Priority: P1.
Depends on: R14.
Unblocks: final player deliverable; this is the intentional task-graph sink.

## Context for a fresh implementer

Workspace: `/Users/tyler/Documents/GitHub/stair-dismount`.
This existing Godot 4.7.2 Compatibility game ships three skateboard crash routes.
The repair preserves articulated injuries, one breaker, traffic cascades, and the treatment story.
R13 built and extracted an identifiable candidate; R14 actually played that exact candidate natively.
R12 verified automated regressions; none of these gates can be inferred from assertion counts alone.
The prior release lives under builds/StairWreck.app and builds/StairWreck-macOS.zip.
Play.command currently prefers that app even if the source has changed.
No Git repository or project AGENTS.md existed at planning time; inspect added instructions.
No upload, external publication, message sending, or paid service is part of this task.
Promoting verified files within this authorized workspace is the intended deliverable.

## Why launch provenance matters

A user can report unchanged bugs after source fixes because Play.command opens an older bundle.
The current old ZIP is healthy; stale content and physical corruption are different diagnoses.
A candidate is valid only for the source/assets digest that was tested.
Building again after native validation would silently create a different unvalidated artifact.
Promote the verified bytes, then verify the promoted artifact identity independently.
Keep a previous release backup so a packaging regression is reversible.

## Launcher contract

A downloaded app/ZIP launches the packaged PCK it contains and displays its build ID in diagnostics.
The workspace Play.command resolves paths relative to itself, including paths with spaces.
When source and app identities match, launch the verified bundled app normally.
When source changed and the local Godot 4.7.2 is available, launch current source explicitly
and print a concise development-source/build-identity message before opening the window.
When source changed and Godot is unavailable, report that the bundled game is older and
provide the exact rebuild/development command; do not silently label it the repaired source.
Supply a separate Development.command or documented command for deliberate source launch.
Do not require the user to decide whether the engine mismatch is safe.
Use the supported installed version or a clear actionable version requirement.
Never inject --test-mode, capture, self-check, or temporary record paths into ordinary play.
Do not erase, relocate, or overwrite the player's user:// records to make launch pass.
A packaged app is runnable without a Godot/Blender installation, as before.

Choose identity-aware launch rather than always preferring source because the standalone
package is the player product, while source edits must not masquerade as the same tested build.
This avoids loading an obsolete release and makes future bug reports reproducible.

## Promotion sequence

1. Read the R14 report and confirm candidate ID, source digest, ZIP digest, and native evidence.
2. Recompute candidate hashes and fail if any artifact changed after native validation.
3. Check current source/assets against the R13 manifest; fail on mismatched edits.
4. Preserve the existing app, ZIP, source ZIP, and manifest in a clearly named prior-release directory.
5. Promote the exact verified candidate app and ZIP without rerunning export.
6. Apply/validate the launcher contract and finalize source README/development commands.
7. Build the source archive after these edits. Runtime inputs must match the validated candidate
   exactly; record a separate full source-deliverable inventory for launchers/docs/tools, excluding
   generated evidence, caches, user data, recursive archives and .beads database/lock files.
   Re-extract the source ZIP and test launcher dry-run matching/stale/missing-app cases.
8. Reverify promoted ZIP CRC, extracted file hashes, PCK identity, and signature.
9. Run the bounded packaged three-route smoke check from the promoted extracted ZIP.
10. Finalize release evidence/package hashes and verify source README matches the archived finalized version.
11. Verify all closed repair beads have concrete acceptance evidence and required gates.
12. Provide links to the final app ZIP and clear launch instructions.

## Documentation contract

README leads with the actual launch path and repaired build version.
Describe fixed observable problems instead of saying world class or bug free.
List supported OS/architecture and the environments actually tested.
Include exact automated suite exit status and candidate/native evidence location.
Record native screenshots separately from historical Blender validation renders.
Do not overwrite old fallback captions to imply those images came from Godot.
State any material remaining visual/audio/platform limitations.
Document campaign save migration/recovery behavior and pending save wording.
Show development launch/rebuild commands without unnecessary internal process detail.
Retain engine and asset license notices in the app and source archive.
No assertion count is presented as proof of fun or blanket correctness.

## Independent acceptance cases

- Re-extract promoted ZIP into a new empty directory and verify every file against the manifest.
- Run ZIP integrity checks and strict ad-hoc codesign verification on the extracted app.
- Compare extracted PCK hash with the exact natively validated candidate PCK.
- Verify app version/build ID and source digest agree with release notes and source ZIP.
- Launch from a directory containing spaces using Play.command fixture dispatch.
- Test matching identities, source-modified identities, missing Godot, and missing app branches.
- Test unsupported Godot version messaging without launching the wrong engine.
- Confirm ordinary launcher invocation contains no test/capture/automation flags.
- Perform one ordinary isolated launch/restart on the final bytes without an automated input driver.
- Confirm the app requires neither Blender nor an installed external Godot to play.
- Reopen a prior-version save fixture through the final package and verify recovery/migration behavior.
- Verify promoted docs never point to a superseded candidate or stale package hash.
- Confirm preserved prior release is intact and can be restored if necessary.

Launcher dispatch tests may use dry-run command reporting; gameplay smoke uses real Godot.
Test path/argument behavior without writing a real player save or spawning obsolete builds accidentally.
Do not mutate the final PCK to add a test script after it was validated.
External scripts may probe exported assets without changing candidate contents.

## Rollback and interruption

If promotion integrity fails, leave the candidate intact and restore prior public paths from backup.
Do not remove the backup until the final verification and deliverable links are complete.
If source changed between validation and promotion, rebuild a new candidate through R13
and rerun the required R14 evidence instead of accepting the old report.
Mark release task incomplete until those mandatory gates finish.
No task is closed because time is short or because a ZIP exists.

## Done and user handoff

Produce final package hashes, source digest, launch smoke log, and the final validation report.
Update repair plan status and task evidence links without deleting the original incident register.
All prerequisites are closed for implemented/verified reasons; no open native gate is hidden.
The user gets a concrete final downloadable workspace artifact, not just a proposed rebuild.
R15 has no child task because it is the release sink, not an orphan investigation.
Close only after exact validated bytes and truthful documentation are delivered.
